name: Florida
summary: Statutes: Online Sunshine (leg.state.fl.us) per-section pages are constructible from the section number and read cleanly by both tools; flsenate.gov is the second official fetch (crawl-delay 10, 429s under load); Justia (2025) and public.law (stale 2024 text) are tier-2. Constitution: one huge page on flsenate/Online Sunshine — WebFetch cannot reach Articles VI-XII, the script can. Court rules: only Florida Bar PDFs, shell-blocked by Cloudflare and cut off by WebFetch after ~100K chars, so most rules (e.g. Civ. P. 1.510) are unreachable. Case law: every flcourts.gov host (Supreme Court, six DCAs) is robots-disallowed and ACIS is a JS app; use Justia (1848-2026, PCAs included) and the FSU archive of Supreme Court opinions. Admin code: flrules.org metadata is fine but rule text is a binary .doc; LII has text but lags (2023 vs 2026 amendments).

citation_map.notes: Florida has no public-domain/vendor-neutral case citation; cases are cited to So./So. 2d/So. 3d (West) or, before reporter publication, to Florida Law Weekly (commercial; S = Supreme Court, D = DCAs) or Westlaw. Florida style (Fla. R. App. P. 9.800) writes DCA courts as '(Fla. 4th DCA 2019)'; Bluebook writes '(Fla. Dist. Ct. App. 2019)': both are matched. Florida statutes are a single code (section = chapter.number), so no code key is needed; statutes are cited as 'Fla. Stat. § 768.81 (2024)' (Bluebook), '§ 768.81, Fla. Stat. (2024)' (Florida style) or 's. 768.81, F.S.' (legislative style). A '§§ 768.71-768.81' range is two sections, not one hyphenated number: the regex takes the first. The Evidence Code is statutory (ch. 90), not a court rule set. Guards: bare 'Rule 1.510', 'rule 3.850' or 'section 90.803' must not route here without a 'Fla.'/'Florida' marker (other states number rules similarly). Docket forms 'SC2022-0378' / '4D2024-0558' (ACIS, 2023 on) and '4D19-0993' / 'SC19-87' (earlier) are Florida-specific in shape but route only with Florida context. PCA (per curiam affirmed without opinion) decisions appear in So. 3d only as table entries and on Justia as one-line opinions; under Jenkins v. State, 385 So. 2d 1356 (Fla. 1980) (from memory, unverified), a citation-free PCA cannot be reviewed by the Supreme Court for conflict, so it is normally final. Since Jan. 1, 2023 there are six DCAs (Sixth DCA, Lakeland). CourtListener ids 'fla' and 'fladistctapp' are from memory and unverified; CourtListener groups all DCAs under one id. Rules Regulating The Florida Bar ('R. Regulating Fla. Bar 4-1.7') and Family Law / Small Claims / Juvenile rules were not probed: no route recorded. Evidence-code cites (§ 90.xxx, Fla. Stat.) match both the Florida Statutes and Evidence Code patterns; both route to the same statute sources, so the double match is harmless. Prose rule forms 'Rule 3.850 of the Florida Rules of Criminal Procedure' and 'Fla. Stat. section 83.56' added after the independent check.

sources.title: Florida Statutes (Online Sunshine)
sources.official_status_evidence: No authentication statement on section pages (footer: 'Copyright 1995-2026 The Florida Legislature'). The sister site flsenate.gov states the online information 'is unverified' and the printed journals/bills should be consulted for official purposes. Florida has not enacted UELMA.
sources.coverage: Current Florida Statutes (header reads 'The 2026 Florida Statutes') plus prior editions 1997-2025 via a StatuteYear parameter; per-section, per-chapter and title-index pages.

access.pattern_rules: Split the section at the dot: chapter = digits before it, subsection = digits after it verbatim (no padding change: 768.81 → '81', 1001.42 → '42', 90.803 → '803'). chapter4 = chapter zero-padded to 4 digits (0090, 0768, 1001). range = the hundred-block of the chapter as 'NNNN-NNNN' (ch. 90 → 0000-0099, ch. 768 → 0700-0799, ch. 1001 → 1000-1099). Prior years: add '&StatuteYear={YYYY}' (verified for 2023; header then reads 'The 2023 Florida Statutes (including Special Session C)'). Whole chapter: …&URL={range}/{chapter4}/{chapter4}.html (very long, see hazards); chapter contents: …/{chapter4}/{chapter4}ContentsIndex.html. http:// redirects to https://.
access.navigation: Not needed for sections (constructible). The title index DOES show section ranges per chapter/part, e.g. 'Part I: GENERAL PROVISIONS (ss. 768.041-768.405)'.

automation.robots_txt: User-agent * — Disallow /employees/ only (Drifter and SemrushBot fully disallowed); /statutes allowed

sources.official_status_evidence: Third-party compilation; edition label only.
sources.coverage: Florida Statutes by year; unversioned URL serves the 2025 edition.

access.pattern_rules: Section dot becomes a hyphen (768.81 → section-768-81). Title (Roman, lower case) and part (Roman, lower case; omitted when the chapter has no parts, e.g. ch. 90) are not in the citation: take them from the Online Sunshine title index, which shows 'Part II … (ss. 768.71-768.81)'. Examples: 768.81 → /title-xlv/chapter-768/part-ii/section-768-81/; 90.803 → /title-vii/chapter-90/section-90-803/. Part ranges: compare the digits after the dot as INTEGERS, not decimals — 83.56 → 56 lies in Part II 'ss. 83.40-83.684' (40-684), not Part I 'ss. 83.001-83.251' (1-251). The title Roman numeral is in the Online Sunshine section-page header ('Title VI'); that header gives no part, so take the part from the title index ranges.

access.pattern_rules: Filename changes on every re-publication (e.g. Civil-Procedure-Rules-06-19-25.pdf → …-10-01-26.pdf). The Bar's index page is unreachable by both tools; find the newest PDF by WebSearch 'site:www-media.floridabar.org <rule set> Rules pdf' and prefer the latest date in the filename.
